ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two blue lines slanting upward to the right, and they have the same pink arrow markings, indicating that they are parallel to each other; there are also two blue lines slanting downward to the right, which are also parallel to each other. ∠1 is located at the upper-left intersection; ∠3 and ∠4 are located at the lower-right intersection, and ∠3 and ∠4 are adjacent, forming a linear pair on a straight line. Reasoning: Since the two groups of slanted lines are respectively parallel, ∠1 and ∠3 are in a corresponding angles/alternate interior angles relationship, so m∠3 = m∠1 = 53°. Also because ∠3 and ∠4 form a linear pair, the sum of their measures is 180°, so m∠4 = 180° - 53° = 127°.

raw_record.question_text: In the figure, $m \angle 1 = 53$. Find the measure of $\angle 4$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as two pairs of parallel slanted lines: the two rising blue lines are parallel to each other, and the two falling blue lines are parallel to each other. Angle 1 is at the upper-left intersection, while angles 3 and 4 are at the lower-right intersection, with angles 3 and 4 adjacent on a straight line. From the parallel-line relationships, angle 1 and angle 3 are corresponding/opposite interior angles in the slanted grid, so m∠3 = m∠1 = 53. Then ∠3 and ∠4 form a linear pair, so m∠4 = 180 - 53 = 127.
